entries.source: Build a School near the colony; assign builders to fetch wood and algae.
The algae grows in the pond. A trained swimmer must enter water to collect it. Keep the School on open land with access for suppliers.
Use algae from the pond
Schools and worker skills
Use the prepared swimmers to build a School, then observe workers learn construction and harvesting.
Your School improved worker skills. Skilled builders unlock upgrades; better harvesting helps maintain an expanding economy.
Build a School in the clearing; assign builders. The colony already has swimmers for algae. Leave access to wood and water. Fruit trees provide prestige resources; food still comes from wheat.
Build a School

Upgrading buildings
Use prepared skilled workers to upgrade a Racetrack and train beyond the first level.
You upgraded a building and used its improved training. Further upgrades repeat this cycle with better Schools, skills, materials and space, up to level 3.

Select the Racetrack, choose Upgrade and assign skilled builders. These workers already learned first-level School skills. Upgrades need extra space and materials, and interrupt the building service. Cancelled upgrades do not count.

Towers and protective walls
Build a supplied tower and protective walls, then test them against one small attack.
Your supplied defenses stopped the practice attack. Towers need stone and walls need gaps so suppliers can keep reaching them.
Build a tower in the marked area; assign builders. Place it near the stone quarry and leave supplier access. No attack starts until the preparation goals are complete.

Guard zones and flag tactics
Scout the practice enemy, prepare a guard zone, defend, then organize a counterattack.
You scouted, defended a guard zone and directed a counterattack. Flag targets request units; radius controls where those units work.
Place an Exploration Flag at the enemy base; assign 1 explorer. Flags request units autonomously. An explorer reveals current activity through fog of war; it may stop to eat.
